notable_absence.finding: INSERTING/OVERWRITING DOCUMENTS states a real, specific mechanism - 'If cbimport encounters an existing record in the bucket that has a document id that matches a record from the input source then it will overwrite the existing record' - but never says which conflict-resolution mechanism governs the overwrite (last-write-wins? CAS check?), unlike cbdatarecovery.md's --force-updates flag which explicitly names 'Couchbase's conflict resolution mechanism' as the default and describes overriding it. No relation minted for the overwrite behavior itself: it is a plain KV upsert with no named mechanism on this page to attach it to.

cross_component_finding: Mirrors cbexport.json's finding: the extraction layer currently carries THREE ids for this one tool - tool:cbimport (minted in cloud/reference/command-line-tools.json, and independently in server/8.0/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/time-series.json), server:cbimport (minted separately in cloud/connect/cli-import-export.json), and capella:import-tool (a DIFFERENT thing - cloud/clusters/data-service/import-data-documents.json's 'Capella Import tool (UI)' is explicitly a browser UI that 'generates cbimport commands or loads data directly', not this CLI binary, so that one is correctly separate and should not be folded in). tool:cbimport and server:cbimport, by contrast, name the identical CLI utility this page documents and should converge - flagging for reconciliation rather than merging here, per this batch's extraction-only scope.
cross_product_finding: Capella's cli-import-export.md states this Server CLI tool is exposed unchanged on Capella clusters, but this page itself (cbimport's own canonical reference) says nothing about Capella and nothing about the SDK-scripted bulk-import alternative (sdk:bulk-import-workflow, already distinguished from this exact tool in the registry's own notes: 'a third bulk-load path...distinct from capella:data-api...and the tool:cbimport/server:cbimport CLI path'). No merge attempted with Capella's Data Tools > Import UI (capella:import-tool) or with the Data API, consistent with the batch instructions: this tool's own page draws no such correspondence, so none is asserted here.
